citation: Niu B.; Al-Menhali A.; Krevor S. The impact of reservoir conditions on the residual trapping of carbon dioxide in Berea sandstone. Water Resources Research 51 (2015).
key_data: Fired Berea; D=3.8 cm; L=20 cm; phi=21%; k=212 mD; PV=47.6 mL. Experimental-design proxy: Swr=0.1699; nw=6; ng=3; Pe=5.5 kPa; lambda=0.6.
evidence_scope: Excellent porous-medium reference but multiphase data are CO2/brine at 25-50 C, not SCW/hydrocarbon.

citation: Krevor S.C.M. et al. Relative permeability and trapping of CO2 and water in sandstone rocks at reservoir conditions. Water Resources Research 48 (2012).
key_data: Berea phi=22.1%; k=914 mD in that specimen; Brooks-Corey Pe=2.5 kPa; Swi=0.11; lambda=0.67.
evidence_scope: Rock/fluid proxy only; lower temperature and different nonwetting fluid.

citation: Oak M.J.; Baker L.E.; Thomas D.C. Three-Phase Relative Permeability of Berea Sandstone. Journal of Petroleum Technology 42 (1990) 1054-1061.
key_data: Water-wet fired Berea; extensive two-/three-phase relative-permeability measurements and saturation-history dependence.
evidence_scope: Best historical three-phase sandstone analogue; not SCW conditions.

citation: Kianinejad A.; Chen X.; DiCarlo D.A. The effect of saturation path on three-phase relative permeability. Water Resources Research 51 (2015) 9141-9164.
key_data: Water-wet sand pack; mean grain 0.25 mm; phi=0.365; k=13 D; long CT-monitored column.
evidence_scope: Controlled packing benchmark; permeability too high to copy directly for SCW.

citation: Moghadasi L. et al. Characterization of two- and three-phase relative permeability of water-wet porous media through X-Ray saturation measurements. Journal of Petroleum Science and Engineering 145 (2016) 453-463.
key_data: Sand-pack phi=0.37; water k=2900 mD; Berea comparison core also measured.
evidence_scope: Useful relative-permeability laboratory reference; not SCW.

citation: Al-Menhali A.S.; Krevor S. Capillarity and wetting of carbon dioxide and brine during drainage in Berea sandstone at reservoir conditions. Water Resources Research 51 (2015).
key_data: Fired homogeneous Berea; water k=212 mD; phi about 21%; capillary/wetting study.
evidence_scope: Supports fired Berea preparation and water-wet analogue, not 380 C wettability.

citation: Pini R.; Benson S.M. Simultaneous determination of capillary pressure and relative permeability curves from core-flooding experiments with various fluid pairs. Water Resources Research 49 (2013).
key_data: Berea MICP entry pressure about 53.5 kPa; demonstrates fluid-pair dependence of scaled capillary pressure.
evidence_scope: MICP is pore-structure evidence; not direct SCW capillary pressure.

citation: Peksa A.E.; Wolf K.-H.A.A.; Zitha P.L.J. Bentheimer sandstone revisited for experimental purposes. Marine and Petroleum Geology 67 (2015).
key_data: Bentheimer phi about 0.21-0.27; permeability about 0.52-3.02 D; homogeneous quartz-rich sandstone.

citation: Kocurek Industries Berea sandstone SS-103 product specification.
key_data: Current listed porosity 18-21%; KCl permeability 80-120 mD; custom laboratory cores.
